definitions.explanation: Basic rights and freedoms to which all humans are entitled.

examples.japanese: {基本的|きほんてき}{人権|じんけん}は{大切|たいせつ}だ。
{人権|じんけん}{問題|もんだい}について{話|はな}し{合|あ}う。
すべての{人|ひと}の{人権|じんけん}が{尊重|そんちょう}されるべきだ。
examples.english: The human rights of all people should be respected.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}では{毎年|まいとし}、{人権|じんけん}について{考|かんが}える{授業|じゅぎょう}がある。
examples.english: At school, there are classes every year where we think about human rights.

notes:
{人権|じんけん} means human rights — the basic rights and freedoms that belong to every person. The kanji combine {人|じん} (person) + {権|けん} (right).

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {人権|じんけん}{侵害|しんがい}: human rights violation
- {人権|じんけん}{団体|だんたい}: human rights organization
- {人権|じんけん}{問題|もんだい}: human rights issue
- {基本的|きほんてき}{人権|じんけん}: fundamental human rights

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {人権|じんけん}を{守|まも}る: to protect human rights
- {人権|じんけん}を{尊重|そんちょう}する: to respect human rights
- {人権|じんけん}を{侵害|しんがい}する: to violate human rights

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese schools hold annual {人権|じんけん}{教育|きょういく} (human rights education) events. The {世界|せかい}{人権|じんけん}{宣言|せんげん} (Universal Declaration of Human Rights) is a commonly referenced document.
